releases.notes:
# Village Quest 2.6.2 — Living Kingdoms

Clearer village adventures, illustrated conversations with travelling friends and more useful quest rewards.

## New features

- Talk to Simon, Lutte and Marius in illustrated quest windows with live objectives, native item tooltips and clear rewards. Raphael has his own harp illustration and conversation page.
- Pin a Journal quest in the tracker, choose whether other tasks stay visible and follow concrete next steps through all five village-story chapters.
- Read your inn’s recorded opening-time progress and remaining operating time.
- Use Simon’s green Wayfarer’s Token for 30 seconds of Speed II, with a shared five-minute cooldown per player and remaining-time messages in chat. Tokens are reusable and freely transferable; existing Simon reward feathers gain the new function.

## Fixes and improvements

- Fix the Guild Wayshrine loot-table error that could stop Minecraft 26.3 from opening or creating worlds (GitHub #7). Minecraft 26.2 keeps its own valid native loot format.
- Inspect actual enchantments, potion effects and both exclusive Lutte tool choices. Friends windows share a fixed size and keep scrolling separate from their action buttons.
- Simon gives three Swiftness II potions (1:30 each) for his first quest. His Weather Tonics remain freely transferable.
- Lutte’s coastal quest rewards an Unbreaking III book. His masterpiece now needs 2 ancient debris, 16 redstone and 8 amethyst shards instead of a netherite ingot; you still choose exactly one tool.
- Green names identify smaller special quest rewards, including the token, Watch Seal and Weather Tonic. Major story artifacts retain gold names; the Watch Seal retains its owner restriction.
- Retain existing story progress, party sharing, saved reward choices and safe inventory delivery. English, German and Spanish guidance matches the updated requirements and effects.

Back up your world before updating and install matching Village Quest versions on client and server. Choose the Runtime JAR for your Minecraft version; Sources are for developers.

**Minecraft 26.3 · Fabric Loader 0.19.5+ · Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3 · Java 25.** Install Village Quest and Fabric API on both client and server.

releases.notes:
# Village Quest 2.6.1 — Living Kingdoms

A smoother journey through Living Kingdoms: more reliable Notice Posts, clearer quests and a better Quest Board.


## Fixes and improvements

- Keep the Daily and Weekly reset timers fully inside the Quest Board parchment, including wrapped text, with the hover area moved to match.
- Place a compact Guild Notice Post when a full Guild Corner has no safe site. Improve forest and existing-village retrofit, recover failed reservations, and prevent removed boards from becoming a renewable item source. Buildings, containers and unloaded areas stay protected.
- Find unlocked Village Quest recipes in the general crafting search. Keep different outputs in separate entries and use any native plank type in Council Seat, Market Desk, Trader Stall and Notice Post recipes.
- Keep two-line quest titles clear of Daily/Solo labels, preserve manual scrolling during updates, and sample the correct top surface on living maps.
- Exclude babies from village quest conversations and introductions. Show reachable building furnishings when a high roof is outside the selected scan while retaining roof and room-separation requirements.
- Follow clearer guidance through all five village-story chapters. Revised English, German and Spanish instructions explain the actual objectives, counters, deliveries, materials, books, equipment and rewards without changing their requirements.

Existing progression is retained. Back up your world before updating and use matching Village Quest versions on client and server. Do not downgrade a world from a newer Minecraft version.

**Minecraft 26.3 · Fabric Loader 0.19.5+ · Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3 · Java 25.** Install Village Quest and Fabric API on both client and server. Use the Runtime JAR as the mod; Sources are provided separately.

releases.notes:
# Village Quest 2.1.1 - Homesteads & Wayfinding

Your own base can finally become part of the village trade network—and the road beyond it is clearer, steadier, and far more configurable.

## New features

- Turn a safe player-built base into a Homestead Trade Post as soon as the Market Charter unlocks the Caravan Ledger, while destinations remain real inhabited vanilla or CTOV villages.
- Survey ocean routes with proper ferry legs, safe shore boarding points, dashed sea lanes, boat markers, and live arrival times. Lakes and rivers still require roads or bridges.
- Keep one stable illustrated map across panning and sessions through deterministic per-world terrain tiles stored in a bounded cache.
- Configure reset timezone, caravan visibility, map quality, HUD/minimap layout, notifications, sounds, markers, and tutorial hints without changing save progress.
- Choose Full, Reduced, or Map only physical caravans while the virtual route economy keeps running normally.
- Use the read-only `/vq diagnose [player]` report to inspect routes, homes, incidents, road quality, traders, and possible stuck or orphaned caravans.
- Toggle the Quest Tracker with `.` and the minimap with `,`, both grouped under `Village Quest` in Controls.
- Enjoy a unified visual pass for all eight active Village Quest tools and relics, including a bespoke Caravan Ledger, Roadwarden Horn, and 32-frame Surveyor's Compass.

## Bug fixes and improvements

- Increased Restless Pens horseback travel to 4,800 blocks and removed the repetitive sound from every distance tick.
- Rebalanced Bakehouse Help so the required wheat naturally covers both bread crafting and the final delivery.
- Added clear Trust milestone bars and corrected when Prosperity becomes available.
- Made map terrain, shading, shorelines, and decorative marks remain visually stable while panning.
- Added player markers to both maps and made all route-map layers respect their visibility settings.
- Made Daily and Weekly resets timezone- and daylight-saving-safe for the actual server location.
- Shortened special-item tooltips, restored the Journal Collection icon, and removed verified unreachable legacy resources.

Available for Minecraft 26.2, 26.1.2, and 1.21.11.
